title: Advancing Hope Act of 2016
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on September 22, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Advancing Hope Act of 2016

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to revise the priority review voucher program for rare pediatric disease medications. (A priority review voucher is a transferable voucher that entitles the holder to have a new drug or biological product application acted upon by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) within six months.) The program is restricted to treatments for serious diseases and is terminated at the end of 2016.

Beginning 90 days after enactment of the bill, a medication sponsor who intends to request a voucher for a rare pediatric disease medication must notify the FDA of that intent upon submission of the application for the medication.

The bill applies to applications submitted to the FDA before enactment of the bill that have not been approved. Applications submitted before October 7, 2012, are not eligible for a voucher.

A voucher may not be issued for a rare pediatric disease product if a voucher was already issued for the medication under another program.

(Sec. 3) The Government Accountability Office must study the effectiveness of awarding priority review vouchers as an incentive for the development of medications for rare pediatric diseases that would not otherwise have been developed.

summary.headline: This law changes the rare pediatric disease priority review voucher program, which lets drug makers speed up FDA review of certain drugs for serious childhood diseases.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to revise a program that gives a transferable voucher to drug sponsors who develop treatments for rare pediatric diseases. A voucher lets its holder have a new drug application reviewed by the FDA within six months. Sponsors must tell the FDA when they submit an application that they plan to request a voucher, starting 90 days after enactment. The law also limits eligibility, bars a second voucher for the same medication, and directs the Government Accountability Office to study whether the program works as intended.

who_it_affects.group: Drug companies developing treatments for rare pediatric diseases
who_it_affects.how: They must notify the FDA when submitting an application if they plan to request a priority review voucher, and applications filed before October 7, 2012 are not eligible.

who_it_affects.group: Families of children with rare serious diseases
who_it_affects.how: The program is limited to treatments for serious diseases, and it is set to end at the end of 2016 under the summary provided.
The agency must receive voucher notices from sponsors and cannot issue a voucher for a product that already received one under another program.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The notification requirement starts 90 days after enactment on September 30, 2016, and the bill applies to pending unapproved applications.
